parchment-rose.$description: Parchment Rose — Page canvas and section backgrounds — the warm off-white ground that gives the whole system its dusty, paper-like atmosphere

specimen-white.$description: Specimen White — Card surfaces and image wells — clean white plates that sit on the parchment canvas, carrying typographic specimens and editorial imagery

ink-brown.$description: Ink Brown — Primary text, headlines, and dominant body copy — the warm near-black that reads as ink rather than pure black against the rose canvas

walnut.$description: Walnut — Navigation text, secondary links, and muted metadata — one step lighter than Ink Brown for hierarchy without leaving the brown family

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Deepest neutral for in-image text and high-contrast moments where Ink Brown isn't dark enough

hairline-ash.$description: Hairline Ash — Subtle border on form inputs and fine dividers — a warm gray that stays in the brown family

dusty-rose.$description: Dusty Rose — Red supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

domainetext.$description: Body text, navigation, links, and all running copy — a transitional serif that carries the editorial, printed-specimen feel. Its old-style figures (onum) and standard ligatures give body text a bookish quality.

dia.$description: ALL-CAPS micro-labels: nav items, category badges, dates, font attributions, and section tags. The ultra-heavy weight plus tight tracking creates a compact, industrial counterpoint to the serif body — a signature pairing that makes even a date stamp feel designed.

domainedisplaynarrow.$description: Editorial headlines, article titles, and the site wordmark. The narrow proportions and high contrast give display type a fashion-magazine authority — it is the voice that announces, never explains.
